text: What is the strongest argument for keeping state out of components?
choices: Component state is stored as strings, which wastes memory compared to primitive fields.
Only one component may hold a given piece of state, so a second view is impossible.
The model can then be tested with no screen, in milliseconds, which means those tests actually run in a build.
Components are recreated on every repaint, so any state stored in them is lost.
explanation: Interface tests need a display, are slow, and break when a button moves — so everything you move out of the view becomes testable and everything you leave in effectively is not. The verified example ran the model to a value of 10 with no view attached. The invariant also then holds no matter which view or listener attempts the change, rather than being duplicated in every handler.
